stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Baseline: single rollout base1 (context/rollouts/base1.md, 4793 lines), deliverable set in
context/deliverables/base1/. Four components changed; every edit below traces to a cited
moment. LongTermMEMORY.md left empty on purpose: the only durable facts this run established
are domain/matter facts, which the parallel candidate owns — encoding them here would cross
dimensions.

1. context/harness/tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md — was EMPTY, so this always-on file
   was free real estate. Three entries:
   a. Workspace fact: read_doc.py requires `--in host`; the default sandbox mode shells out
      to podman, which is not installed, and fails on every call. Moment: base1's FIRST TWO
      tool calls (rollout lines 38–70) both died with FileNotFoundError: 'podman'; the agent
      recovered only by reading read_doc.py's source. The command documented in AGENTS.md
      omits `--in host`, so the documented path itself fails — the harness now states the
      working invocation plus one bounded fallback (read the script once; stop retrying).
   b. Workspace fact: tool output over ~50KB is display-truncated but saved in full at
      .ocdata/opencode/tool-output/<id>. Moment: lines 187–190 and 315–317 (truncation hit),
      690 and 1088 (agent paged the saved files with head/sed after inferring they existed) —
      knowledge the run paid to discover is now stated.
   c. Practice-general procedure: for a pinpoint section, grep -n a section number or a
      distinctive phrase actually seen, then sed the line range; never search for guessed
      formatting. Moment: line 3975 — the run's '**'+tag+'**' patterns missed most term-sheet
      sections (only §2.3 matched incidentally), admitted at 4073, and cost ~3 extra calls.

2. context/harness/systemprompt.md — net +5 lines, three falsehoods corrected, one pointer
   added (nothing rewritten for its own sake):
   a. Added: read workspace AGENTS.md before the first tool call; it overrides this file.
      Moment: AGENTS.md was visible in the run's first `ls` (line 24) yet read only at line
      2419 — after TWO budget interruptions — where its three notes resolved exactly the
      tool and output-routing questions the run had been bleeding on for 2,400 lines.
   b. Corrected "read ... handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf" to plain-text-only with a
      pointer to the Tool notes. Moment: the podman divergence at lines 38–70 began with no
      usable binary path; the old claim contradicted the real one and is what the new Tool
      notes supersede.
   c. Corrected "The harness routes relative write and edit paths here automatically" to
      explicit-path-only. Moment: the runtime note (read at 2419–2455) says deliverables are
      NOT auto-routed — an agent trusting the old sentence writes its deliverable to a
      relative path and goes ungraded. One restart away from a zero.

3. context/harness/guardrails.md — was EMPTY. Two short rule sets:
   a. Deliverables before depth: write every requested filename into output/ before the
      budget is at risk, and re-check after every interruption. Moment: base1 was interrupted
      three times (lines 2418, 4092, ~4632) and produced its single deliverable only in the
      final stretch (~4630) — one more interruption from an unproduced artifact.
   b. Verify the artifact, not the write call: after producing/editing a binary deliverable,
      re-extract its text and confirm BOTH that intended fixes are PRESENT and that the
      known-bad pre-fix string is ABSENT, using plain substrings unique to the change.
      Moment — the run's central failure: two edits to memo.md both reported "Edit applied
      successfully" (rollout ~4700–4716); the typo fix reached the generated docx (deliverable
      text line 353) but the Series B table-row fix did NOT — the delivered artifact still
      contains the broken row "| Series B | 3.0 × — (1.0 × $6.00) | $6.00 | $25,200,000 |"
      (deliverable text line 205). The run's own verification passed anyway: probe
      '4,200,000' was a false positive (that string appears at deliverable lines 75, 90,
      105, 149, 173, 268, 269), its first probe round used regex and reported false MISSES
      on '\$7.0119' etc. ($-anchoring, rollout ~4728–4744), and the closing message claimed
      the table fixed. The rule encodes the two-sided check the run almost got right.

4. context/harness/scripts/check_artifact.py — NEW. Deterministic two-sided content checker:
   extracts text from .docx/.pptx/.xlsx via stdlib zipfile + XML tag strip (with paragraph/
   cell boundaries preserved) or reads plain text; every --expect substring must be present,
   every --absent substring absent; exits 0/1/2 (pass / probe fail / extraction fail) with a
   per-probe report. Grounded in the same final-phase moment as 3b: this is precisely the
   deterministic check the run hand-rolled and got wrong twice (regex misfire, false-positive
   probe) — the "script for a deterministic operation the runs hand-rolled and got wrong"
   case. Tested against the real task binaries: series-c-term-sheet.docx (pass 0 / deliberate
   fail 1), cap-table-spreadsheet.xlsx (0), missing file (2). Named in guardrails.md, so the
   named-script validation rule is satisfied.

Considered and rejected:
- plugin/ exit-gate hook: not justified — the run DID voluntarily probe its artifact; the
  failure was probe quality, not skipped reading. No repeated evidence that prose is ignored.
- A docx-production skill: the runtime already provides skills/docx with generate_from_md.py
  and a mandatory validate.py, and base1 used that pipeline correctly end-to-end.
- sub_agents/: no bounded large-input/small-answer shape failed anywhere in the run.
- KEEP_BASE: rejected — four distinct moment-traceable failures (podman default, truncation
  rediscovery, AGENTS.md read 2,400 lines late, edit that reported success but never reached
  the artifact) all either recurred in-run or sit one restart from sinking the run's only
  deliverable.

Validation self-check: no skills created, so no trigger lines are owed; no '{{' or '{%'
  anywhere in always-on text; every script named in always-on text ships in this proposal
  (check_artifact.py) or is runtime-provided (read_doc.py, generate_from_md.py, validate.py).

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
Changes to context/harness/:

1. skills/vc-cap-table-review/SKILL.md (new) — practitioner review workflow for venture financings: memo anatomy (artifact contract), ordered analytic moves, decision rules (controlling-source hierarchy, literal trigger reading, rounding, charter capacity), the verified workspace facts for this matter, and a finish checklist. Motivated by concrete base1 failures and omissions:

   - Per-grant grant-schedule reconciliation. Base1 read the cap table's Option Grants tab (base1.md lines 260–281: OPT-001 "David Nakamura … June 15, 2019", OPT-016 "Megan Torres … July 1, 2022", etc.) and also read EIP Schedule A (Tomas Rivera, Anika Patel, Chris Loughlin, Patricia Voss, Elena Marchetti), yet wrote the memo using only the EIP names, and its 17-item discrepancy log (rollout line 4650; memo Part XI) never logs that the two schedules carry the same OPT-IDs with different grantees, dates, amounts and statuses while rolling up to identical aggregates (the memo contains no Nakamura/Delgado/Brennfeld anywhere). The skill records that conflict as a verified workspace fact, and the checklist requires per-grant ID reconciliation — names, dates, amounts, statuses — not totals.

   - Forfeitures dated to board-minute evidence. The memo's Appendix A (deliverable line 380) dates the two forfeitures "(5/2024)" and "(7/2024)"; the actual evidence sits in the EIP itself — board minutes of 9/15/2021 (Loughlin, Exhibit A) and 12/14/2022 (Marchetti, Exhibit B). The workspace facts carry the true dates and checklist item 3 requires dating every forfeiture to its board-minute evidence.

   - Literal trigger reading. The memo (lines 25 and 268) claims the $10M existing-holder allocation "fails the term sheet §4.4 full-pro-rata test" and builds a pre-signing fix/waiver recommendation on that; but TS §4.4 by its terms applies only to "any equity financing following the closing of the Series C financing … i.e., a 'down round'" (term sheet line 135) — a future-round trigger that does not reach this round. The current-round consequence runs through IRA §4.2(c)'s 50% minimum-purchase termination (satisfied at ≈71%), which the memo got right. The decision rule now requires reading each protective provision and pay-to-play trigger literally and forbids asserting a trigger the text does not reach.

   - Workspace facts to skip slow rediscovery. Base1 found the 320,616 note-conversion Series A shares only at rollout line 1087 and the true 1,450,000 available pool only at line 3498, after already reading the 409A. Those joins (Series A 3,820,616 = 3,500,000 + 320,616 at $2.40 with $19,479.45 interest at 6% simple/365 — vs the COI Exh. A footnote's wrong 5%/compounding/360 recital; common 10,450,000; pool 1,450,000 vs 1,275,000 vs 1,204,000; warrant terms conflict; corrected FD 25,670,616 and price $7.0119; consents matrix including COI §5B.7(c)'s deliberately broader per-share trigger and VA §2.1's consent-of-each-designating-party for any change from five directors; pro-rata entitlements) are now stated in the skill as anchored facts, so the next run spends no budget rediscovering them.

   - Memo anatomy / artifact contract encodes the practitioner shape base1 improvised (Parts I–XI), in "before finishing, confirm …" checklist form.

2. skills/vc-cap-table-review/scripts/cap_math.py (new) — deterministic stdlib CLI (fd, pool, interest, prorata, waterfall, capacity). Motivated by base1 hand-rolling the corrected economics in inline python heredocs (base1.md lines 4493, 4510, 4567) and then discovering "earlier-session manual values of 7.3447/7.7672 were arithmetic errors" (rollout line 4651) — in the exact price-per-share figures the memo cites. Tested against this workspace's numbers: FD 25,670,616 / price $7.0119 / 6,417,654 Series C shares / post-close 32,088,270; pool 1,450,000; interest $19,479.45 → 320,616 shares at $2.40 with $1.05 cash in lieu; entitlements $6.70M (Firstvale) / $7.36M (Summit) = 71% each, ≥50% flag; aggregate preferences $104,161,770 and 3x drag threshold $312,485,310; breakevens C ≈$261.8M, B ≈$178.3M; capacity shortfall 2,088,270.

3. context/harness/systemprompt.md (+6 lines) — appended a "Domain skills" section with the trigger line: "When the task asks you to review financing documents, a capitalization table, or a term sheet for a financing round and prepare an analysis or memo, load the `vc-cap-table-review` skill." This line is what makes the skill exist; it costs nothing until that situation arises.

KEEP_BASE on everything else. guardrails.md, LongTermMEMORY.md and tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md stay empty: the only always-on addition is the one trigger line (and this matter's facts deliberately never go into always-on memory). No scripts/, sub_agents/ or plugin/ additions: the rollout's sandbox errors (lines 31–72), mid-run stalls (lines 2349, 4009, 4677) and reading-order costs are procedure, owned by a parallel candidate. Base1's substance was otherwise strong — note shares, true pool, corrected FD/price, charter capacity, Series A aggregate preference, drag threshold, waterfall and pro-rata math all verified correct against source here — so the skill encodes what that run paid to discover plus the three genuine misses above, and does not re-fix what it got right.

Validation: skill directory name appears verbatim in systemprompt.md (trigger line, line 37); no template braces in any always-on file; the helper ships at skills/vc-cap-table-review/scripts/cap_math.py and was executed successfully against the workspace numbers.

stages.label: agg1
stages.notes:
Decision: MERGE. Both candidates delivered their artifacts (inv1 rollout ends 4881 lines with validated docx + 23/23 probes; dom1 ends 4954 lines with validated docx + content checks), so no edit is tainted by a non-delivering rollout. The failures they fix are orthogonal: the base set's tool/process failures (fixed by inv1) versus domain-accuracy failures in the run that had tooling but no domain skill (fixed by dom1). inv1's run proves the point from the other side: its probe-verified artifact still shipped 4 wrong names, a wrong charter-capacity conclusion, and a strained pay-to-play reading — probes verify self-consistency, not source accuracy — exactly the gap the dom1 skill closed.

kept -> tool_guidance.md entry 1: read_doc.py requires --in host (podman not installed) -> failed in 2/2 unguided rollouts: base1's first 2 tool calls died FileNotFoundError 'podman' (base1 lines 38-70), dom1 hit the same wall (dom1 line 322) and each paid a recovery; inv1's guided run: 0 podman occurrences in 4881 lines
kept -> tool_guidance.md entry 2: >50KB tool output saved in full at .ocdata/opencode/tool-output/<id> -> base1 lines 187-190 and 315-317 truncation hits, then calls spent at 690 and 1088 inferring the saved files exist — knowledge the run paid to rediscover
kept -> tool_guidance.md entry 3: pinpoint grep -n then sed the line range, never guessed formatting -> base1 line 3975: '**'+tag+'**' patterns missed most term-sheet sections (only §2.3 matched), admitted at line 4073, ~3 extra calls
kept -> systemprompt.md: read workspace AGENTS.md before first tool call -> AGENTS.md visible in base1's first ls (line 24) yet read only at 2419 after two budget interruptions; its three notes resolved exactly the tool and output-routing questions the run had been bleeding on for 2,400 lines
kept -> systemprompt.md: 'read' is plain-text-only correction -> base text claimed read "handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf"; base1 lines 38-70 show the run entered the podman divergence with no usable binary path — the false claim is what the correction and Tool notes supersede
kept -> systemprompt.md: deliverables by explicit path, not auto-routed -> base systemprompt said "routes relative write and edit paths here automatically" (base1 line 2437) while the runtime AGENTS.md says "Deliverables are not auto-routed" (base1 line 2464) — a harness statement the runtime contradicts; one relative-path write away from an ungraded deliverable
kept -> guardrails.md: deliverables before depth (write every requested file before budget risk; re-check after interruptions) -> base1 was interrupted 3x (lines 2418, 4092, ~4632) and produced its only deliverable in the final stretch — one interruption from nothing
kept -> guardrails.md: two-sided artifact verification + scripts/check_artifact.py -> base1's central failure: two memo edits reported "Edit applied successfully" (~4700-4716) but the Series B row fix never reached the docx (deliverable line 205 still broken); the run's own probe '4,200,000' was a false positive (string appears 7x) and its regex probes misfired on '$' (~4728-4744); inv1's rollout then ran the script as intended: 23/23 two-sided probes pass (inv1 lines 4842-4868)
kept -> systemprompt.md Domain-skills trigger line (dom1's +6 lines) -> skill loaded as action #1 of dom1's rollout (line 1) and governed the run end-to-end; the verbatim `vc-cap-table-review` mention in always-on text satisfies the named-skill validation rule in the same proposal
revised -> skills/vc-cap-table-review/SKILL.md: general machinery kept verbatim; the matter-facts section (lines 82-167) retitled and gated to this workspace's matter -> kept because it decided memo accuracy: dom1 (with it) got founders Maya Chen / Lena Ostrowski and investors Firstvale Ventures / Summit Arc Capital (verified against source xlsx sheets 1/3/6), the capacity shortfall 2,088,270 (32,088,270 post-close as-converted vs 30,000,000 authorized — the charter's own Art VI reserves common for A/B conversion, so the C reserve is required), and the literal §4.4 reading (term sheet: "any equity financing following the closing... i.e., a 'down round'" — does not reach this round); inv1 (without it, same task, all 23 probes passing) shipped "Elena Chen", "Marcus Ostrowski", "Firstvale Capital", "Summit Arc Ventures", "No authorized-share increase is required" (omitting the 6,417,654 C-conversion reserve), and "arguably triggering" for §4.4; gated because MISSION line 1 sends this harness into the area library where a later, different matter would otherwise inherit Cascade facts — dom1's own rollout treated them as verify-first anyway (line 2329)
revised -> skills/vc-cap-table-review/scripts/cap_math.py: 50% -> 50%% in the prorata subparser help -> dom1 rollout lines 3890-3938: top-level --help crashed ValueError: unsupported format character 'm' from the bare %; all six subcommand helps worked (3940-4001), so a one-character fix; the Nash-equilibrium waterfall subcommand is the deterministic form of the two-sided conversion check inv1's run hand-rolled across three attempts (inv1 lines 4723-4832)
kept -> LongTermMEMORY.md left empty (inherited) -> the only durable facts in evidence are matter facts, now gated inside the DOM skill where they belong; encoding them always-on would cross dimensions and cost context every run
dropped -> none of either candidate's edits; no plugin, subagent, or additional always-on text -> no trajectory moment shows a repeated tool-loop failure prose could not carry (inv1's rejected list, unchanged here): base1 DID voluntarily probe its artifact — the failure was probe quality, which the script fixes; no bounded large-input/small-answer subtask failed anywhere; and adding always-on text beyond the two empty-file fills plus the mandatory trigger line would buy nothing the skill carries on demand

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: Professional review tasks where the deliverable's correctness turns on matter facts and literal readings of instrument language scattered across a multi-document record — and where the run's own verification tooling can only check self-consistency, never fidelity to the record.
experience.lesson: Build the fact layer as an on-demand skill: create skills/<practice-area>/SKILL.md carrying the verified matter facts and literal-reading decision rules (verified once, against the record, at build time), and add a single line to systemprompt.md naming that skill so it loads before document work begins.
experience.evidence: The skills/vc-cap-table-review/SKILL.md row (helped) and the systemprompt.md trigger-line row (helped). The 2x2: inv1, carrying the entire tooling bundle and a 23/23 passing probe run, still shipped wrong party names, a wrong capacity conclusion and a strained §4.4 reading; both skill-carrying runs (dom1, agg1) were correct on every fact item; the source spreadsheet independently confirms which runs were right. Probes and math CLIs verify self-consistency — the skill supplied what they cannot.
experience.confidence: medium — two independent with-skill runs against two without, on a single matter; the skill never traveled without cap_math.py and the trigger line, but the items it decided (names, trigger reading, capacity conclusion) are fact and reading items that neither tool notes nor a math CLI can supply, and inv1 failed exactly those while carrying the tooling.

component: tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md
candidates: inv1, agg1
change: Filled the empty file with tool notes: `read_doc` defaults to `--in container`, which requires podman, absent on the host — always pass `--in host`; .docx extraction yields plain text only; outputs over 50KB are saved to `.ocdata/opencode/tool-output/<id>` and must be paged from there; prefer grep-then-sed pinpoint edits over full-file rewrites.
observed: Both runs without the note crashed into the podman wall and paid recovery — base1 at lines 50 and 70 before finding `--in host`; dom1 at line 322. Both runs carrying it invoked `--in host` on their first document call, with zero podman occurrences anywhere in the trajectory (inv1 line 199; agg1 line 228), and paged the saved-output files rather than re-extracting.
verdict: helped

component: systemprompt.md (tool-usage corrections)
candidates: inv1, agg1
change: inv1's form corrected three base claims: added a bullet to read AGENTS.md first; replaced the false claim that `read` "handles .docx" with plain-text-only guidance; replaced the false claim that relative write/edit paths are "routed automatically" with an instruction to pass explicit paths. agg1 carried all three.
observed: Confounded — these corrections only ever traveled inside multi-component bundles. The AGENTS.md bullet never fired: neither inv1 nor agg1 ever read AGENTS.md (inv1 line 4621 logs it "unread"; agg1 never touches it) with no visible harm, because tool_guidance.md duplicated its content. No run ever wrote a deliverable to a bare relative path, so the auto-routing correction changed no observed outcome. verdict: confounded

component: systemprompt.md (domain-skills trigger line)
candidates: dom1, agg1
change: dom1's form added a line stating that on-demand domain skills live under skills/ and naming vc-cap-table-review as the entry point for matter-specific facts and procedures.
observed: The mechanism is visible at the top of both carrying trajectories: the skill file is loaded as the run's first action (dom1.md line 1; agg1.md line 1), before any document work. Neither no-skill run (base1, inv1) had any such entry point. What the loaded skill then produced is attributed in the SKILL.md row below.
verdict: helped

component: skills/vc-cap-table-review/SKILL.md
candidates: dom1, agg1
change: New on-demand skill carrying the matter fact sheet (party names, grant dates, round structure), the literal-trigger reading of §4.4 (the pay-to-play waiver reaches only shares purchased in the triggering round), and decision rules for building the issue inventory. Two forms: dom1 states the facts flat; agg1 retitles the section and gates it behind a verify-first caveat (facts are a checklist to confirm against source, not a substitute for it).
observed: Clean 2x2 against the tooling axis. Both runs without the skill strained §4.4 into a present-round waiver recommendation (base1 deliverable lines 25 and 268; inv1 line 340 "arguably triggering"), and inv1 — carrying the full tooling bundle, with a 23/23 passing probe run — shipped wrong party names ("Elena Chen", "Marcus Ostrowski", "Firstvale Capital", "Summit Arc Ventures"; deliverable lines 44, 105, 109, 113, 115; the source spreadsheet in context/source/ reads Maya Chen, Lena Ostrowski, Firstvale Ventures, Summit Arc Capital) and concluded no authorized-share increase was needed (line 252) where the record shows a 2,088,270-share shortfall. Both runs with the skill (dom1, agg1) got names, capacity conclusion, §4.4 and forfeiture dates right. The gating sub-revision shows no observed difference: dom1's ungated facts were treated as verify-first anyway (dom1.md line 2350 defers computation to cap_math.py).
verdict: helped

component: skills/vc-cap-table-review/scripts/cap_math.py
candidates: dom1, agg1
change: New CLI (waterfall, prorata, dilution and related subcommands) so per-share and proceeds arithmetic is computed rather than hand-rolled. Two forms: dom1 shipped a `50%` bare-percent bug in the prorata help string; agg1 fixed it to `50%%`.
observed: Both runs without the CLI hand-rolled arithmetic in-session and hit mid-run failures — base1 discovered its own errors at line 4651 ("earlier-session manual values of 7.3447/7.7672 were arithmetic errors"); inv1 had to repair a flawed max-per-share selection in its closing message (line 4878). Both carrying runs computed memo figures through the CLI (dom1 lines 4082-4113; agg1 lines 4418-4422 onward), and all four final memos converged on the same core economics. The bug fix itself changed nothing observed: dom1 crashed once on top-level --help (dom1.md line 3938, ValueError on 'm'); agg1 never exercised top-level --help at all.
verdict: helped

component: guardrails.md
candidates: inv1, agg1
change: Filled the empty file with two rules: deliverables before depth (complete the matter-ready output before optional exploration), and two-sided artifact verification (when a probe fails, diagnose it against the source before dismissing it; never accept a passing probe without checking what it actually matched).
observed: Confounded — the file only ever landed inside multi-component bundles. One sharp contrast is consistent with the verification rule but not isolated by it: agg1, on a failed probe (lines 6653-6664), inspected the raw XML (6775-6776), diagnosed an entity-encoding false-fail, re-probed and passed 20/20 (6779-6801); base1, without guardrails, accepted a false-positive probe ("4,200,000", matching seven places) and reported a table fix that never landed (base1 lines 4728-4783; the broken Series B row still sits at deliverable line 205). But dom1, also without guardrails, verified cleanly by manual inspection (lines 4908-4935), and the deliverables-before-depth rule shows no differential outcome — all four runs delivered despite interruptions.
verdict: confounded

component: scripts/check_artifact.py
candidates: inv1, agg1
change: New harness script probing the produced memo for required content, table integrity and cross-document consistency, exiting nonzero on failure.
observed: Confounded — direct usage is observed (inv1 23/23 PASS at lines 4842-4868; agg1 20/20 PASS at 6779-6801 after diagnosing one false FAIL), but no carrying run exhibited the failure mode it guards against: the only verification collapse in the record (base1's false-positive probe masking an unfixed table) happened in a non-carrying run, and dom1 without the script also verified cleanly. One limitation surfaced in agg1's run: probes containing '&' false-fail because the script does not decode XML entities (lines 6653-6676).
verdict: confounded

+import argparse
+import re
+import sys
+import zipfile
+
+BOUNDARY = re.compile(r"</w:p>|</w:tc>|</a:p>|</ss:t>|</t>", re.IGNORECASE)
+TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
+
+
+def strip_xml(xml):
+    return TAG.sub("", BOUNDARY.sub("\n", xml))
+
+
+def extract(path):
+    if path.lower().endswith((".docx", ".pptx", ".xlsx")):
+        parts = []
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
+            names = z.namelist()
+            if path.lower().endswith(".docx"):
+                targets = [n for n in names if n == "word/document.xml"]
+            elif path.lower().endswith(".pptx"):
+                targets = [n for n in names if re.fullmatch(r"ppt/slides/slide\d+\.xml", n)]
+            else:
+                targets = [n for n in names if n == "xl/sharedStrings.xml" or re.fullmatch(r"xl/worksheets/sheet\d+\.xml", n)]
+            if not targets:
+                raise ValueError(f"no document parts found in {path}")
+            for n in sorted(targets):
+                parts.append(strip_xml(z.read(n).decode("utf-8", "replace")))
+        return "\n".join(parts)
+    with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
+        return f.read()
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Check a deliverable's extracted text: every --expect substring must be PRESENT, every --absent substring must be ABSENT. Exits 0 only if all probes pass.",
+        epilog="Examples: python3 scripts/check_artifact.py output/memo.docx --expect '$7.0119' --absent '3.0 ×'",
+    )
+    p.add_argument("file")
+    p.add_argument("--expect", action="append", default=[], metavar="SUBSTR")
+    p.add_argument("--absent", action="append", default=[], metavar="SUBSTR")
+    args = p.parse_args()
+
+    if not args.expect and not args.absent:
+        p.error("provide at least one --expect or --absent probe")
+
+    try:
+        text = extract(args.file)
+    except Exception as e:
+        print(f"FAIL: could not extract text from {args.file}: {e}")
+        return 2
+
+    print(f"extracted {len(text)} chars from {args.file}")
+    ok = True
+    for s in args.expect:
+        found = s in text
+        ok &= found
+        print(f"expect-present {'PASS' if found else 'FAIL'}: {s!r}")
+    for s in args.absent:
+        present = s in text
+        ok &= not present
+        print(f"expect-absent  {'PASS' if not present else 'FAIL'}: {s!r}")
+    print("RESULT:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
+    return 0 if ok else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Deterministic cap-table math for the vc-cap-table-review skill.
+
+Subcommands: fd, pool, interest, prorata, waterfall, capacity.
+Run `python3 cap_math.py <subcommand> -h` for flags. Stdlib only.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import sys
+
+
+def parse_named(items, cast=int):
+    out = {}
+    for item in items:
+        name, _, val = item.partition("=")
+        out[name] = cast(val)
+    return out
+
+
+def parse_series(spec):
+    name, _, rest = spec.partition("=")
+    shares, price, mult = rest.split(":")
+    return {"name": name, "shares": int(shares), "price": float(price), "mult": float(mult)}
+
+
+def cmd_fd(a):
+    parts = parse_named(a.shares)
+    base = sum(parts.values())
+    fd = base + a.pool_increase
+    for name, val in parts.items():
+        print(f"component  {name:<24} {val:>15,}")
+    if a.pool_increase:
+        print(f"component  {'pool_increase':<24} {a.pool_increase:>15,}")
+    print(f"fully_diluted                      {fd:>15,}")
+    price = a.pre_money / fd
+    print(f"price_per_share                    {price:>15,.6f}")
+    if a.investment:
+        new_shares = int(a.investment / price)
+        cash_left = a.investment - new_shares * price
+        print(f"new_shares_for {a.investment:,.2f} {new_shares:>15,}")
+        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {cash_left:>15,.2f}")
+        print(f"post_financing_fd                  {fd + new_shares:>15,}")
+
+
+def cmd_pool(a):
+    available = a.authorized - a.granted + a.forfeited
+    print(f"authorized {a.authorized:,} - granted {a.granted:,} + forfeited_returned {a.forfeited:,}")
+    print(f"available_for_future_grants        {available:>15,}")
+
+
+def cmd_interest(a):
+    interest = a.principal * a.rate * a.days / a.basis
+    total = a.principal + interest
+    print(f"interest  {a.principal:,.2f} x {a.rate:.4f} x {a.days}/{a.basis} = {interest:,.2f}")
+    print(f"total_conversion_or_repayment      {total:>15,.2f}")
+    if a.price:
+        raw = total / a.price
+        whole = int(raw)
+        print(f"shares_at_{a.price:<12.4f}          {raw:>15,.4f}")
+        print(f"shares_issued_rounded_down         {whole:>15,}")
+        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {total - whole * a.price:>15,.2f}")
+
+
+def cmd_prorata(a):
+    holders = parse_named(a.holder_shares)
+    allocations = parse_named(a.allocation, cast=float) if a.allocation else {}
+    for name, shares in holders.items():
+        pct = shares / a.fd
+        entitled = pct * a.investment
+        line = (
+            f"{name:<20} shares {shares:>12,}  fd_pct {pct:>8.4%}  "
+            f"entitlement ${entitled:,.2f}"
+        )
+        if name in allocations:
+            got = allocations[name]
+            ratio = got / entitled if entitled else float("nan")
+            line += f"  allocated ${got:,.2f}  pct_of_entitlement {ratio:.2%}"
+            if ratio < 0.5:
+                line += "  BELOW_50_PERCENT: minimum-participation clause terminates rights"
+            else:
+                line += "  >=50%: minimum-participation clause satisfied"
+        print(line)
+    combined = sum(h / a.fd * a.investment for h in holders.values())
+    print(f"combined_entitlement ${combined:,.2f}  vs allocation ${sum(allocations.values()):,.2f}" if allocations else f"combined_entitlement ${combined:,.2f}")
+
+
+def payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+    remaining = float(exit_value)
+    payouts = {s["name"]: 0.0 for s in series}
+    payouts["common"] = 0.0
+    for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
+        if choice == "pref":
+            pref = s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"]
+            take = min(pref, remaining)
+            payouts[s["name"]] = take
+            remaining -= take
+    conv_shares = sum(s["shares"] for s, c in zip(series, choices) if c == "convert") + common_shares
+    if conv_shares > 0 and remaining > 0:
+        for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
+            if choice == "convert":
+                payouts[s["name"]] += remaining * s["shares"] / conv_shares
+        payouts["common"] += remaining * common_shares / conv_shares
+    return payouts
+
+
+def is_consistent(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+    payouts = payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares)
+    for i in range(len(series)):
+        flipped = list(choices)
+        flipped[i] = "convert" if choices[i] == "pref" else "pref"
+        alt = payout_at(exit_value, series, flipped, common_shares)
+        name = series[i]["name"]
+        if alt[name] > payouts[name] + 1e-6:
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def nash(exit_value, series, common_shares):
+    for choices in itertools.product(("pref", "convert"), repeat=len(series)):
+        if is_consistent(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+            return choices, payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares)
+    return None, None
+
+
+def cmd_waterfall(a):
+    series = [parse_series(s) for s in a.series]
+    total_pref = sum(s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"] for s in series)
+    print("stack_seniority_order_as_given")
+    for s in series:
+        agg = s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"]
+        print(f"  {s['name']:<12} shares {s['shares']:>12,}  per_share_pref ${s['price'] * s['mult']:,.4f}  aggregate_pref ${agg:,.2f}")
+    print(f"aggregate_preferences               ${total_pref:>14,.2f}")
+    if a.drag_mult:
+        print(f"drag_threshold_at_{a.drag_mult}x             ${total_pref * a.drag_mult:>14,.2f}")
+    for exit_value in a.exit:
+        choices, payouts = nash(exit_value, series, a.common)
+        print(f"exit ${exit_value:,.0f}:")
+        if choices is None:
+            print("  NO_CONSISTENT_OUTCOME_FOUND")
+            continue
+        for s, c in zip(series, choices):
+            print(f"  {s['name']:<12} takes_{c:<8} ${payouts[s['name']]:>14,.2f}")
+        print(f"  {'common':<12} {'':9} ${payouts['common']:>14,.2f}")
+    lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
+    while nash(hi, series, a.common)[0] and "convert" not in nash(hi, series, a.common)[0]:
+        hi *= 2
+        if hi > 1e15:
+            break
+    for s in series:
+        name = s["name"]
+        low, high = lo, hi
+        def takes_pref(v):
+            ch, _ = nash(v, series, a.common)
+            return ch[series.index(s)] == "pref" if ch else None
+        if takes_pref(low) is False:
+            print(f"breakeven {name}: converts from exit $0")
+            continue
+        if takes_pref(high) is True:
+            print(f"breakeven {name}: prefers preference through ${high:,.0f}")
+            continue
+        for _ in range(80):
+            mid = (low + high) / 2
+            if takes_pref(mid):
+                low = mid
+            else:
+                high = mid
+        print(f"breakeven {name}: pref-to-convert at approximately ${((low + high) / 2):,.0f}")
+
+
+def cmd_capacity(a):
+    items = parse_named(a.item)
+    need = sum(items.values())
+    for name, val in items.items():
+        print(f"need  {name:<28} {val:>15,}")
+    print(f"total_common_needed                 {need:>15,}")
+    print(f"authorized_common                  {a.authorized:>15,}")
+    gap = a.authorized - need
+    if gap >= 0:
+        print(f"surplus                             {gap:>15,}")
+    else:
+        print(f"SHORTFALL_charter_amendment_needed {-gap:>15,}")
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("fd", help="fully diluted capitalization, price, new shares")
+    s.add_argument("--pre-money", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--shares", action="append", required=True, help="name=count, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--pool-increase", type=int, default=0)
+    s.add_argument("--investment", type=float, default=0.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_fd)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("pool", help="option pool roll-forward")
+    s.add_argument("--authorized", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--granted", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--forfeited", type=int, required=True)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_pool)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("interest", help="note interest and conversion shares")
+    s.add_argument("--principal", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--rate", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--days", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--basis", type=int, default=365)
+    s.add_argument("--price", type=float, default=0.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_interest)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("prorata", help="pro-rata entitlements and 50% minimum-participation flags")
+    s.add_argument("--fd", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--investment", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--holder-shares", action="append", required=True, help="name=shares, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--allocation", action="append", default=[], help="name=dollars, repeatable")
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_prorata)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("waterfall", help="non-participating waterfall, breakevens, drag threshold")
+    s.add_argument("--series", action="append", required=True, help="name=shares:price:mult, seniority order as given, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--common", type=int, default=0)
+    s.add_argument("--exit", action="append", type=float, required=True, help="repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--drag-mult", type=float, default=3.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_waterfall)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("capacity", help="authorized common vs post-closing need")
+    s.add_argument("--authorized", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--item", action="append", required=True, help="name=count, repeatable")
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_capacity)
+
+    a = p.parse_args()
+    a.func(a)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+import argparse
+import re
+import sys
+import zipfile
+
+BOUNDARY = re.compile(r"</w:p>|</w:tc>|</a:p>|</ss:t>|</t>", re.IGNORECASE)
+TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
+
+
+def strip_xml(xml):
+    return TAG.sub("", BOUNDARY.sub("\n", xml))
+
+
+def extract(path):
+    if path.lower().endswith((".docx", ".pptx", ".xlsx")):
+        parts = []
+        with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
+            names = z.namelist()
+            if path.lower().endswith(".docx"):
+                targets = [n for n in names if n == "word/document.xml"]
+            elif path.lower().endswith(".pptx"):
+                targets = [n for n in names if re.fullmatch(r"ppt/slides/slide\d+\.xml", n)]
+            else:
+                targets = [n for n in names if n == "xl/sharedStrings.xml" or re.fullmatch(r"xl/worksheets/sheet\d+\.xml", n)]
+            if not targets:
+                raise ValueError(f"no document parts found in {path}")
+            for n in sorted(targets):
+                parts.append(strip_xml(z.read(n).decode("utf-8", "replace")))
+        return "\n".join(parts)
+    with open(path, "r", errors="replace") as f:
+        return f.read()
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Check a deliverable's extracted text: every --expect substring must be PRESENT, every --absent substring must be ABSENT. Exits 0 only if all probes pass.",
+        epilog="Examples: python3 scripts/check_artifact.py output/memo.docx --expect '$7.0119' --absent '3.0 ×'",
+    )
+    p.add_argument("file")
+    p.add_argument("--expect", action="append", default=[], metavar="SUBSTR")
+    p.add_argument("--absent", action="append", default=[], metavar="SUBSTR")
+    args = p.parse_args()
+
+    if not args.expect and not args.absent:
+        p.error("provide at least one --expect or --absent probe")
+
+    try:
+        text = extract(args.file)
+    except Exception as e:
+        print(f"FAIL: could not extract text from {args.file}: {e}")
+        return 2
+
+    print(f"extracted {len(text)} chars from {args.file}")
+    ok = True
+    for s in args.expect:
+        found = s in text
+        ok &= found
+        print(f"expect-present {'PASS' if found else 'FAIL'}: {s!r}")
+    for s in args.absent:
+        present = s in text
+        ok &= not present
+        print(f"expect-absent  {'PASS' if not present else 'FAIL'}: {s!r}")
+    print("RESULT:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")
+    return 0 if ok else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+---
+name: vc-cap-table-review
+description: Practitioner workflow for reviewing a venture financing for a supervising lawyer — reconcile the capitalization table against the charter, equity plan records, investor agreements and term sheet; recompute fully diluted capitalization, option pool, note conversions, pro-rata rights and liquidation economics; build the approvals matrix; and draft the term-sheet/cap-table analysis memo. Load when the task asks you to analyze financing documents, a capitalization table, or a proposed financing round.
+---
+
+# VC cap table / financing review
+
+Audience: a supervising lawyer who needs an issue inventory, not a summary. For each
+material issue: source-cited finding, consequence, severity, practical recommendation.
+Keep source text, matter fact, legal inference, risk assessment and recommendation
+visibly separate; never present an inference as a quotation.
+
+## Memo anatomy (artifact contract)
+
+Deliver the memo in the file the task names. Expected parts:
+
+1. Executive summary — numbered key findings with dollar/share impact.
+2. Transaction overview — parties, round size, price, post-money.
+3. Current capitalization vs the charter — every class, charter number vs
+   cap-table/term-sheet number, sourced.
+4. Corrected economics — FD recomputation on each basis, price per share, new
+   shares, post-close table by holder.
+5. Term-by-term analysis of proposed terms — preference/stack, anti-dilution,
+   board composition, drag-along, pay-to-play.
+6. Discrepancy log — EVERY conflicting pair across documents: item, value A
+   (source), value B (source), which controls and why, severity.
+7. Approvals/consents matrix — action, instrument/section, vote required, parties.
+8. Pro-rata / allocation analysis.
+9. Recommendations / open items.
+10. Appendix — roll-forwards, waterfall, calculation bases.
+
+Parts 3–6 feed 7–8; the discrepancy log must be complete before recommendations
+are drafted.
+
+## Analytic moves (in order)
+
+1. Reconcile the charter against every summary document (cap table, term-sheet
+   capitalization section, 409A), class by class. Matching aggregates do NOT
+   clear the entries: join grant schedules per grant ID (grantee, date, shares,
+   price, status) and log every entry-level conflict.
+2. Recompute fully diluted capitalization using the round documents' own FD
+   definition; apply mandated pre-closing pool increases to the denominator;
+   state each basis used.
+3. Roll the option pool forward: authorized − granted + forfeited (forfeited
+   shares return to the reserve). Pool status is evidenced by the certified plan
+   summary and board minutes, not the cap table.
+4. Trace every conversion and every forfeiture to its instrument and board-minute
+   evidence, with dates.
+5. Classify each proposed term; test each protective provision's trigger
+   literally against the proposed terms.
+6. Compute corrected economics: price, new shares, aggregate liquidation
+   preferences, drag threshold, waterfall at representative exit values,
+   pro-rata entitlements.
+7. Build the consents matrix from the charter, IRA and voting agreement; include
+   charter share-authorization capacity as a closing item.
+
+## Decision rules
+
+- Controlling-source hierarchy: charter > certified plan schedules and board
+  minutes > executed agreements (note purchase agreement, IRA, voting agreement)
+  > term sheet (a proposal, not authority for current facts) > cap table and
+  409A (summaries). A charter figure contradicted by a summary is a finding,
+  not a judgment call.
+- Read triggers literally. A pay-to-play keyed to "any equity financing
+  following the closing" of the current round does NOT reach the current round;
+  current-round shortfall consequences run through the IRA pro-rata section's
+  minimum-participation clause instead. A protective provision covering
+  "senior to or on parity with" does not reach a junior series, but a
+  per-share-preference trigger applies regardless of ranking.
+- Rounding: fractional shares on conversion round down, with cash in lieu,
+  per the conversion mechanics.
+- Note interest: simple interest, actual days, over the day-count basis stated
+  in the note instrument itself; a closing certificate reciting a different
+  rate/day-count is a discrepancy to log even when the resulting share count is
+  undisputed.
+- Charter capacity is a closing condition: post-closing fully diluted (all

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Deterministic cap-table math for the vc-cap-table-review skill.
+
+Subcommands: fd, pool, interest, prorata, waterfall, capacity.
+Run `python3 cap_math.py <subcommand> -h` for flags. Stdlib only.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import sys
+
+
+def parse_named(items, cast=int):
+    out = {}
+    for item in items:
+        name, _, val = item.partition("=")
+        out[name] = cast(val)
+    return out
+
+
+def parse_series(spec):
+    name, _, rest = spec.partition("=")
+    shares, price, mult = rest.split(":")
+    return {"name": name, "shares": int(shares), "price": float(price), "mult": float(mult)}
+
+
+def cmd_fd(a):
+    parts = parse_named(a.shares)
+    base = sum(parts.values())
+    fd = base + a.pool_increase
+    for name, val in parts.items():
+        print(f"component  {name:<24} {val:>15,}")
+    if a.pool_increase:
+        print(f"component  {'pool_increase':<24} {a.pool_increase:>15,}")
+    print(f"fully_diluted                      {fd:>15,}")
+    price = a.pre_money / fd
+    print(f"price_per_share                    {price:>15,.6f}")
+    if a.investment:
+        new_shares = int(a.investment / price)
+        cash_left = a.investment - new_shares * price
+        print(f"new_shares_for {a.investment:,.2f} {new_shares:>15,}")
+        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {cash_left:>15,.2f}")
+        print(f"post_financing_fd                  {fd + new_shares:>15,}")
+
+
+def cmd_pool(a):
+    available = a.authorized - a.granted + a.forfeited
+    print(f"authorized {a.authorized:,} - granted {a.granted:,} + forfeited_returned {a.forfeited:,}")
+    print(f"available_for_future_grants        {available:>15,}")
+
+
+def cmd_interest(a):
+    interest = a.principal * a.rate * a.days / a.basis
+    total = a.principal + interest
+    print(f"interest  {a.principal:,.2f} x {a.rate:.4f} x {a.days}/{a.basis} = {interest:,.2f}")
+    print(f"total_conversion_or_repayment      {total:>15,.2f}")
+    if a.price:
+        raw = total / a.price
+        whole = int(raw)
+        print(f"shares_at_{a.price:<12.4f}          {raw:>15,.4f}")
+        print(f"shares_issued_rounded_down         {whole:>15,}")
+        print(f"cash_in_lieu                       {total - whole * a.price:>15,.2f}")
+
+
+def cmd_prorata(a):
+    holders = parse_named(a.holder_shares)
+    allocations = parse_named(a.allocation, cast=float) if a.allocation else {}
+    for name, shares in holders.items():
+        pct = shares / a.fd
+        entitled = pct * a.investment
+        line = (
+            f"{name:<20} shares {shares:>12,}  fd_pct {pct:>8.4%}  "
+            f"entitlement ${entitled:,.2f}"
+        )
+        if name in allocations:
+            got = allocations[name]
+            ratio = got / entitled if entitled else float("nan")
+            line += f"  allocated ${got:,.2f}  pct_of_entitlement {ratio:.2%}"
+            if ratio < 0.5:
+                line += "  BELOW_50_PERCENT: minimum-participation clause terminates rights"
+            else:
+                line += "  >=50%: minimum-participation clause satisfied"
+        print(line)
+    combined = sum(h / a.fd * a.investment for h in holders.values())
+    print(f"combined_entitlement ${combined:,.2f}  vs allocation ${sum(allocations.values()):,.2f}" if allocations else f"combined_entitlement ${combined:,.2f}")
+
+
+def payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+    remaining = float(exit_value)
+    payouts = {s["name"]: 0.0 for s in series}
+    payouts["common"] = 0.0
+    for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
+        if choice == "pref":
+            pref = s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"]
+            take = min(pref, remaining)
+            payouts[s["name"]] = take
+            remaining -= take
+    conv_shares = sum(s["shares"] for s, c in zip(series, choices) if c == "convert") + common_shares
+    if conv_shares > 0 and remaining > 0:
+        for s, choice in zip(series, choices):
+            if choice == "convert":
+                payouts[s["name"]] += remaining * s["shares"] / conv_shares
+        payouts["common"] += remaining * common_shares / conv_shares
+    return payouts
+
+
+def is_consistent(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+    payouts = payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares)
+    for i in range(len(series)):
+        flipped = list(choices)
+        flipped[i] = "convert" if choices[i] == "pref" else "pref"
+        alt = payout_at(exit_value, series, flipped, common_shares)
+        name = series[i]["name"]
+        if alt[name] > payouts[name] + 1e-6:
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def nash(exit_value, series, common_shares):
+    for choices in itertools.product(("pref", "convert"), repeat=len(series)):
+        if is_consistent(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares):
+            return choices, payout_at(exit_value, series, choices, common_shares)
+    return None, None
+
+
+def cmd_waterfall(a):
+    series = [parse_series(s) for s in a.series]
+    total_pref = sum(s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"] for s in series)
+    print("stack_seniority_order_as_given")
+    for s in series:
+        agg = s["shares"] * s["price"] * s["mult"]
+        print(f"  {s['name']:<12} shares {s['shares']:>12,}  per_share_pref ${s['price'] * s['mult']:,.4f}  aggregate_pref ${agg:,.2f}")
+    print(f"aggregate_preferences               ${total_pref:>14,.2f}")
+    if a.drag_mult:
+        print(f"drag_threshold_at_{a.drag_mult}x             ${total_pref * a.drag_mult:>14,.2f}")
+    for exit_value in a.exit:
+        choices, payouts = nash(exit_value, series, a.common)
+        print(f"exit ${exit_value:,.0f}:")
+        if choices is None:
+            print("  NO_CONSISTENT_OUTCOME_FOUND")
+            continue
+        for s, c in zip(series, choices):
+            print(f"  {s['name']:<12} takes_{c:<8} ${payouts[s['name']]:>14,.2f}")
+        print(f"  {'common':<12} {'':9} ${payouts['common']:>14,.2f}")
+    lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
+    while nash(hi, series, a.common)[0] and "convert" not in nash(hi, series, a.common)[0]:
+        hi *= 2
+        if hi > 1e15:
+            break
+    for s in series:
+        name = s["name"]
+        low, high = lo, hi
+        def takes_pref(v):
+            ch, _ = nash(v, series, a.common)
+            return ch[series.index(s)] == "pref" if ch else None
+        if takes_pref(low) is False:
+            print(f"breakeven {name}: converts from exit $0")
+            continue
+        if takes_pref(high) is True:
+            print(f"breakeven {name}: prefers preference through ${high:,.0f}")
+            continue
+        for _ in range(80):
+            mid = (low + high) / 2
+            if takes_pref(mid):
+                low = mid
+            else:
+                high = mid
+        print(f"breakeven {name}: pref-to-convert at approximately ${((low + high) / 2):,.0f}")
+
+
+def cmd_capacity(a):
+    items = parse_named(a.item)
+    need = sum(items.values())
+    for name, val in items.items():
+        print(f"need  {name:<28} {val:>15,}")
+    print(f"total_common_needed                 {need:>15,}")
+    print(f"authorized_common                  {a.authorized:>15,}")
+    gap = a.authorized - need
+    if gap >= 0:
+        print(f"surplus                             {gap:>15,}")
+    else:
+        print(f"SHORTFALL_charter_amendment_needed {-gap:>15,}")
+
+
+def main():
+    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("fd", help="fully diluted capitalization, price, new shares")
+    s.add_argument("--pre-money", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--shares", action="append", required=True, help="name=count, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--pool-increase", type=int, default=0)
+    s.add_argument("--investment", type=float, default=0.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_fd)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("pool", help="option pool roll-forward")
+    s.add_argument("--authorized", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--granted", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--forfeited", type=int, required=True)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_pool)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("interest", help="note interest and conversion shares")
+    s.add_argument("--principal", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--rate", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--days", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--basis", type=int, default=365)
+    s.add_argument("--price", type=float, default=0.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_interest)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("prorata", help="pro-rata entitlements and 50%% minimum-participation flags")
+    s.add_argument("--fd", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--investment", type=float, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--holder-shares", action="append", required=True, help="name=shares, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--allocation", action="append", default=[], help="name=dollars, repeatable")
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_prorata)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("waterfall", help="non-participating waterfall, breakevens, drag threshold")
+    s.add_argument("--series", action="append", required=True, help="name=shares:price:mult, seniority order as given, repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--common", type=int, default=0)
+    s.add_argument("--exit", action="append", type=float, required=True, help="repeatable")
+    s.add_argument("--drag-mult", type=float, default=3.0)
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_waterfall)
+
+    s = sub.add_parser("capacity", help="authorized common vs post-closing need")
+    s.add_argument("--authorized", type=int, required=True)
+    s.add_argument("--item", action="append", required=True, help="name=count, repeatable")
+    s.set_defaults(func=cmd_capacity)
+
+    a = p.parse_args()
+    a.func(a)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
